_comment: Single source of truth for PhenoMAP's own product information. The five About pages (frontend/src/views/about/*.vue) render from this file, and the chat-service's PRODUCT_FACTS (chat-service/prompts.py, loaded via chat-service/product_facts.py) is generated from this same file -- so PhenoMAP Chat's answers about PhenoMAP itself can never drift from what the site actually shows. Edit this file, not the .vue files or prompts.py, when this information changes.

identity.main_job: help users explore PhenoMAP's phenotype-metabolite-module knowledge graph through entity lookup, graph relationship retrieval, path queries, module enrichment, and evidence-linked summaries

introduction.hero_tagline: PhenoMAP is a phenotype-aware metabolic module atlas: it brings dysregulated metabolic modules from public human metabolomics studies, ontology-normalized phenotypes, and their metabolites together in one searchable knowledge graph.
introduction.overview_heading: Comparing metabolic dysregulation across studies at module scale.
overview_paragraphs: Untargeted LC-MS features vary with analytical platforms and processing workflows, so they are hard to compare between studies. Dysregulated metabolic modules identified by FeatureMAP capture biochemical relationships that can be shared across datasets, which makes them a practical common unit for comparing metabolic alterations across heterogeneous studies.

PhenoMAP applies a standardized TidyMass-FeatureMAP workflow to public human untargeted LC-MS metabolomics studies and links every resulting module to the study it came from, the phenotype that study investigated, and the metabolites that define it. Users can start from a phenotype, a study accession, a module, or a metabolite and follow the graph to related evidence in other studies.

graph_structure.label: Relationships
graph_structure.value: investigated, reported in, member of (core / supporting / contextual), connected with, and similar to

graph_structure.label: Graph Store
graph_structure.value: Neo4j knowledge graph served through the PhenoMAP API

pipeline_steps.title: Curate Public Studies
pipeline_steps.body: Human untargeted LC-MS studies from Metabolomics Workbench and MetaboLights are included when they provide MS1-level raw data and sample metadata that define group comparisons. MS/MS spectra are used when available but are not required. Multi-group designs are split into pairwise comparisons against a reference group.

pipeline_steps.title: Generate Modules
pipeline_steps.body: Raw data are processed with the TidyMass pipeline, differential analysis is run for each comparison, and dysregulated modules are identified with FeatureMAP and annotated in fast mode (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B). Studies yielding at least one dysregulated module are retained, giving 501 studies.

pipeline_steps.title: Normalize Phenotypes
pipeline_steps.body: An LLM-assisted workflow (GPT-4.1) extracts the principal phenotype from each study description, assigns it to one of nine categories, and maps it to category-specific ontology terms. Ambiguous, missing, or biologically inconsistent mappings are reviewed manually, giving 326 standardized phenotypes.

pipeline_steps.title: Build The Graph
pipeline_steps.body: Studies, phenotypes, modules, and metabolites are loaded into Neo4j with their relationships, including module-to-module similarity edges for cross-study comparison.

node_types.title: Study
node_types.body: A public metabolomics study, keeping its repository provenance (Metabolomics Workbench or MetaboLights accession) and experimental context.

node_types.title: Phenotype
node_types.body: An ontology-normalized biological or clinical variable assigned to one of nine categories.

node_types.title: Module
node_types.body: A FeatureMAP-derived dysregulated metabolic module, with its structured functional annotation.

node_types.title: Metabolite
node_types.body: A metabolite in the human metabolic reaction network (MRN) used by FeatureMAP.

relationships.title: investigated
relationships.body: Connects a study to the phenotype it investigated.

relationships.title: reported in
relationships.body: Connects a module to the study in which it was identified.

relationships.title: member of
relationships.body: Connects a metabolite to a module, labeled core (anchor metabolites), supporting (other prioritized metabolites), or contextual (remaining module metabolites).

relationships.title: connected with
relationships.body: Connects two metabolites linked by a reaction in the metabolic reaction network.

relationships.title: similar to
relationships.body: Connects two modules whose similarity score is at least 0.7. The score combines the similarity of their functional annotations with the overlap of member metabolites, chemical classes, and pathway coverage.

analysis_functions.title: Entity Search
analysis_functions.body: Find studies, phenotypes, modules, and metabolites by name, keyword, external database identifier, or stable PhenoMAP identifier. Each result opens a node-detail page with its properties and neighboring records.

analysis_functions.title: Path Query
analysis_functions.body: Find how two entities are connected. The query returns the study, phenotype, and module nodes on all paths up to a user-defined maximum length.

analysis_functions.title: Module Enrichment
analysis_functions.body: Test whether a metabolite list obtained outside FeatureMAP, such as differential metabolites from annotated untargeted data or a targeted assay, is over-represented in PhenoMAP modules, without reanalyzing feature-level data. Each module is represented by its core and supporting metabolites, the background is their union across all modules, and significance is assessed with a one-sided hypergeometric test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. By default, modules with FDR < 0.05 and at least two overlapping metabolites are reported.

analysis_functions.title: PhenoMAP Chat
analysis_functions.body: Ask questions in natural language. Each question is assigned to a query type, the matching PhenoMAP function is called, and the answer is written from the returned records, with every cited study, phenotype, module, and metabolite linked to its PhenoMAP identifier. Chat runs on your own SiliconFlow or OpenAI API key.

analysis_functions.title: Community Submission
analysis_functions.body: Submit your own study. Submissions are reviewed and processed through the same pipeline before being included in a future release, and submitted files are stored separately from the public graph.

data_access: The graph can be explored on this website and downloaded as flat graph tables for reuse. It is stored in Neo4j; entity search, node detail, path query, and graph summary are served by a Go backend API; module enrichment runs in an R Plumber service that calls the original FeatureMAP analysis function; and PhenoMAP Chat is a Python FastAPI service that uses the same graph and enrichment APIs. The interface is built with Vue 3 and Vite.

chatbot_mechanism.heading: How PhenoMAP Chat works
paragraphs: PhenoMAP Chat is a tool-calling assistant, not a text search over documents. For questions about PhenoMAP's own data (an entity, a relationship, an enrichment result), it calls the same search / node-detail / path / enrichment operations that power this website, reads the real results, and answers only from what those calls returned, citing each entity's Lab_ID.
For questions about PhenoMAP Chat or the PhenoMAP project itself, it does not call those tools -- it answers directly from PhenoMAP's own published product information (this same data).

release_notes.title: Initial PhenoMAP release
release_notes.body: First public release of the PhenoMAP knowledge graph and web interface, covering 501 studies, 326 phenotypes in nine categories, 12,929 dysregulated modules, and 9,730 metabolites.

release_notes.title: Graph-backed exploration
release_notes.body: Searchable Study, Phenotype, Module, and Metabolite entities with relationship-level browsing and module similarity edges.

release_notes.title: Analysis workflows
release_notes.body: Entity search, path query, module enrichment, and PhenoMAP Chat (with your own API key) against the current graph.

release_notes.title: Community submissions
release_notes.body: User-contributed studies are reviewed and processed through the same pipeline before inclusion in future releases.
